race_context: Salem Community Schools is in Washington County. It serves Gibson, Jefferson, Monroe and Washington townships, and its schools share a campus on the northwest edge of Salem {wc_salem}. Its schools are Bradie Shrum Elementary, Salem Middle School and Salem High School {scs_board}. State counts show 1,655 students in 2023-24, 1,592 in 2024-25 and 1,551 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}.

Leadership: Luke Dean, a 2001 Salem High School graduate and former teacher, coach and administrator, is superintendent {scs_dean}. Dr. Terry Goodin served as interim superintendent from July 1, 2025 {scs_goodin}. May and June 2026 minutes still list Goodin as interim superintendent and Dean as associate superintendent, and the July 13, 2026 minutes list Dean as superintendent {scs_min_may}{scs_min_jun}{scs_min_jul}. The board hired Dr. April Holder as assistant superintendent on June 8, 2026 {scs_min_jun}{scs_holder}.

The board has seven members serving four-year terms; three seats are filled in one election and the other four two years later {scs_board}. In 2024 the county clerk's office listed four at-large Salem seats on the November ballot {wslm_2024_filing}. (The district's board page still says members are elected in the May primary; the 2024 seats were on the November ballot {scs_board}{wslm_2024_filing}.) Officers are Allison Ezzell (president), Becky Humphrey (vice president) and Rebecca White (secretary); the other members are Brent Minton, Ty Sweeney, Rodney Brough and Steve Motsinger {scs_board}. The district's pages for members elected in 2024, such as Ty Sweeney, list terms of Jan. 1, 2025 to Dec. 31, 2029 {scs_sweeney}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the district lists terms ending Dec. 31, 2026 for Rodney Brough, Steve Motsinger and Rebecca White, which points to three at-large seats {scs_brough}{scs_motsinger}{scs_white}. Brough is on the 2026 ballot; Motsinger and White are not, so at least two new members will join the board {in_list}. The state list shows 'vote for 1'; this guide did not find the Washington County sample ballot to confirm how many candidates voters may choose {in_list}.
Ballot labels: Aaron (Spud) Schocke, Tom Fultz and Tyler Hubbard are listed as Republicans, and LaShawna Spurgeon and Rodney Brough as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

Facilities and bond spending: in June and August 2026 the board approved payments from its 2021 and 2025 bonds. These covered roofing and lighting work, tennis court lights, a scoreboard, signs, prep and design work for a sports complex, and repayment for two buses bought in June 2026 {scs_min_jun}{scs_min_aug}. All passed 6-0. On June 8, 2026 the board also approved resolutions on a fourth lease amendment, its building corporation, construction bids and bond disclosures, after a public hearing at which no one spoke {scs_min_jun}.

Staffing: at the June 8, 2026 meeting a member of the audience raised staffing concerns with the board {scs_min_jun}. On Aug. 10, 2026, board member Brent Minton called the number of transportation resignations 'concerning' {scs_min_aug}. The board renewed LifeSpring contracts for a school-based mental health therapist and an on-campus health clinic for 2026-27 {scs_min_may}.
Academics: in 2025-26 Salem Middle School added an ILEARN prep period twice a week and an incentive program to raise test scores, the principal said {scs_ilearn}.

Safety: Salem received a $51,892 Secured School Safety Grant in 2025 {wslm_safety}. On Aug. 10, 2026 the board accepted the donation of a school resource officer vehicle from the City of Salem {scs_min_aug}.

Budget and taxes: on Aug. 10, 2026 the board approved advertising its budget timeline {scs_min_aug}. This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law SEA 1 affects Salem's budget, and no Salem referendum.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of this race.
